stories.headline: Google DeepMind launches AlphaGenome 2, predicting DNA variant effects in specific cell types

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2 on November 11, 2026, a model that predicts how DNA sequences and their variants affect specific human cell types.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we are announcing AlphaGenome 2, our next-generation model that predicts how DNA sequences and their variations impact specific human cell types

key_facts.fact: The model was trained on more than 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues and identifies nearly twice as many variants that change gene expression as DeepMind's previous model.
key_facts.excerpt: AlphaGenome 2 identifies nearly twice as many variants that change gene expression in cells, compared to our previous state-of-the-art model. Trained on more than 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues

key_facts.fact: On the TenK10K dataset of 28 immune cell types, AlphaGenome 2 identified 30% of causal variants versus 16% for the original AlphaGenome, and 43% of directional gene effects versus 23%.
key_facts.excerpt: AlphaGenome 2 reliably identified nearly twice as many causal variants (30% vs. 16%) and directional gene effects (43% vs. 23%) as the original AlphaGenome fine-tuned on single-cell data

key_facts.fact: AlphaGenome 2 is a conditional model that adapts to new single-cell experiments from just a few dozen cells without retraining, and adds DNA methylation predictions.
key_facts.excerpt: Scientists can upload a single-cell RNA-seq snapshot of gene activity from just a few dozen cells ... The model predicts the same core experimental readouts ... but also DNA methylation, a widely requested readout.

key_facts.fact: The model covers 637 human and 311 mouse cell types it was trained on, according to Nature.
key_facts.excerpt: The model also isn't limited to making predictions in the 637 types of human and 311 mouse cells it was trained with.

key_facts.fact: AlphaGenome 2 is available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API, with a private preview for commercial research.
key_facts.excerpt: Google says it is making AlphaGenome 2 available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API from today, with a limited 'private preview' for commercial research.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini Decision 1, a model that scores choices instead of generating text

key_facts.fact: Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API on November 11, 2026, powered by a new model, Gemini Decision 1 (gemini-decision-1), available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're introducing the Gemini Decisions API, a new endpoint for fast, closed-set decisions powered by our new Gemini Decision 1 model (gemini-decision-1), available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.

key_facts.fact: The model evaluates up to 1,000 yes/no, multiple-choice and rubric questions against one multimodal input of up to 256K tokens in a single forward pass, with 150-250 ms end-to-end latency.
key_facts.excerpt: You can pass one multimodal input across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs (up to 256K tokens) along with up to 1,000 independent questions ... returning probabilities and confidence scores in 150-250 ms end-to-end latency

key_facts.fact: Pricing is $0.10 per 1M input tokens with zero output tokens billed.
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini Decision 1 is priced at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0 for output tokens

key_facts.fact: Google targets the small branching calls inside agents: routing, policy checks, tool selection and grading.
key_facts.excerpt: For developers, this targets the small branching calls inside agents: routing, policy checks, tool selection and grading.

key_facts.fact: The launch puts Google in a market with TypeSafe's Jev, OpenAI's Decisions API running on GPT-6 Luna, and Amazon's Strands Decider.
key_facts.excerpt: That puts Google into a market where TypeSafe's Jev already handles inexpensive classification, OpenAI's Decisions API runs on GPT-6 Luna, and Amazon's Strands Decider gives developers the option to run the model on their own infrastructure.

stories.headline: AWS releases AWS Emulator, a local cloud stand-in written and maintained entirely by AI agents

key_facts.fact: AWS released AWS Emulator on November 11, 2026, a local emulator of AWS services that developers and coding agents can run on their own machines with no AWS account and no service fee.
key_facts.excerpt: Starting today, you can use AWS Emulator to build and test AWS applications on your computer or in your continuous integration (CI) environment ... with no deployments or AWS account required.

key_facts.fact: AWS says thousands of autonomous AI agents wrote every line of code and the team has not written or reviewed any of it.
key_facts.excerpt: The emulator was written entirely by autonomous agents. Our team hasn't written or reviewed any of the code.

key_facts.fact: Three teams of agents run on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: one writes fidelity tests checked against real AWS, one files issues for failures, and one fixes them, one agent per issue; hundreds of agents fix thousands of issues a day.
key_facts.excerpt: The agents run on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in three teams ... Goldberg wrote that hundreds of agents now fix thousands of issues a day.

key_facts.fact: The emulator is built from more than 400 API models covering more than 200 AWS services.
key_facts.excerpt: It's built from more than 400 API models covering more than 200 AWS services.

key_facts.fact: The source code is published on GitHub under a CC0 public-domain dedication; AWS warns it does not evaluate IAM policies and should not be used for security testing.
key_facts.excerpt: Don't use the emulator to test whether your application is secure. It doesn't evaluate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies and resource-based policies the way AWS does

stories.headline: United Airlines bans third-party AI agents from booking flights; CEO wants no 'another middleman'

key_facts.fact: United Airlines said on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, it would restrict unauthorized third-party AI agents from its digital platforms, directly and via travel agencies and aggregators, citing data security.
key_facts.excerpt: United Airlines said on Wednesday it would restrict AI bots' access to its digital platforms, citing data security ... both directly through its digital platforms and indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators

key_facts.fact: United's November 11 contract-of-carriage revision bans the use of AI agents to make, modify or service a ticket, even under human supervision, and lets United cancel such reservations.
key_facts.excerpt: Rule 6.J.6 bans: The use of AI Agents to make, modify or service a Ticket ... Human supervision or approval doesn't circumvent that. And its Rule 5.H gives United the right to cancel reservations

key_facts.fact: CEO Scott Kirby said: 'To be honest, I don't want to create another middleman.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'To be honest, I don't want to create another middleman,' United CEO Scott Kirby said at an event on Tuesday, according to the Journal.

key_facts.fact: Agents can still display United flights and prices but cannot complete the transaction; United cites possible FAA and DOT rule violations, such as automated check-in skipping the hazardous-materials acknowledgment.
key_facts.excerpt: These automated AI actions have the potential to violate FAA and DOT regulations - as an example, flight check-in requires human acknowledgment that bags do not contain banned substances like explosives.

key_facts.fact: Agent bookings made before November 11, 2026 will not be canceled.
key_facts.excerpt: agent bookings made prior to November 11, 2026 will not be canceled

key_facts.fact: Amazon has blocked Meta's AI agent Muse while Walmart partnered with it, and Expedia and Booking work with OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon has blocked Meta's AI agent Muse, while Walmart has partnered with it. Meanwhile, online travel firms such as Expedia and Booking are working with ChatGPT-parent OpenAI.

stories.headline: Tencent's Pony Ma tells staff half the workforce will shift to AI-native businesses

key_facts.fact: In his annual anniversary speech, Tencent founder Pony Ma said he is willing to redeploy half of the company's roughly 100,000-strong workforce to AI-native businesses.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent Holdings Ltd's billionaire founder Pony Ma said he's willing to deploy half of his troops to AI-native businesses, urging his 100,000-strong workforce to embrace an era-defining technology.

key_facts.fact: Ma compared core businesses to an army and AI efforts to a navy: 'The army must leverage AI to maximise its efficiency, while we redeploy 50% of our personnel to the navy to support AI-native businesses.'
key_facts.excerpt: "The army must leverage AI to maximize its efficiency, while we redeploy 50% of our personnel to the navy to support AI-native businesses," he said, according to people with knowledge of the event.

key_facts.fact: Ma also called for a nimbler structure with less mid-tier management; Tencent had 115,927 employees as of June.
key_facts.excerpt: Ma, 55, also called for a nimbler corporate structure with less mid-tier management ... As of June, Tencent reported 115,927 employees, up from 111,221 a year earlier.

key_facts.fact: Tencent PR director Zhang Jun said on Weibo on November 12 that rumors of a 50% layoff are 'completely untrue' and that the remarks describe a reallocation of resources for the AI era.
key_facts.excerpt: 腾讯公关总监张军星期四（11月12日）在微博发文说 ... 这是公司资源适应AI时代的重新调度 ... '该说法完全不属实'

key_facts.fact: The remarks were made during a live-streamed event marking Tencent's 28th anniversary on November 11.
key_facts.excerpt: During a live-streamed annual event to mark the Shenzhen-based company's 28th anniversary yesterday, its leadership signaled the need to accelerate organizational reform

stories.headline: Applied Intuition in talks to raise $1.5B at about $30B valuation, led by General Catalyst

key_facts.fact: Applied Intuition, which develops autonomous-vehicle software and works as a defense contractor, is in talks to raise at least $1.5 billion in a round led by General Catalyst, Bloomberg reported on November 11, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Applied Intuition Inc., a defense contractor developing technology for autonomous vehicles, is in talks to raise at least $1.5 billion in a new funding round led by General Catalyst

key_facts.fact: The deal would value the startup at roughly $30 billion pre-money, double its June 2025 valuation; General Catalyst plans to invest $250 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is expected to value the startup at roughly $30 billion, not including the money raised, doubling what it was worth in June 2025 ... General Catalyst plans to invest $250 million in the round

key_facts.fact: Applied Intuition targets fiscal 2026 revenue above $560 million, up about 19% from $474 million, and forecasts more than $1 billion in 2027 and $1.8 billion by 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Applied Intuition is targeting fiscal 2026 revenue of more than $560 million, representing roughly 19% growth over the $474 million booked in the prior year ... surpass $1 billion in 2027 and reach $1.8 billion by 2028.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2017, the company builds automation operating systems and simulation tools for defense, trucking and construction.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2017, the Silicon Valley startup specializes in automated operating systems and simulation tools tailored for industries ranging from defense and trucking to construction.

stories.headline: AI sales-agent startup Rox raises $100M Series B at $1.3B valuation to take on Salesforce

key_facts.fact: Rox announced a $100 million Series B at a $1.3 billion valuation on November 11, 2026, co-led by General Catalyst and March Capital.
key_facts.excerpt: Rox ... today announced a $100 million Series B financing at a $1.3 billion valuation. The round is co-led by General Catalyst and March Capital

key_facts.fact: Existing investors Sequoia Capital and Factory increased their stakes, and Databricks Ventures and Prosperity7 Ventures joined.
key_facts.excerpt: with existing investors Sequoia Capital and Factory doubling down on their investment, alongside new investors including Databricks Ventures and Prosperity7 Ventures

key_facts.fact: Rox says annual recurring revenue grew more than 10x in its first year in market and net revenue retention exceeds 700% across enterprise customers.
key_facts.excerpt: In its first year in market, Rox has grown annual recurring revenue by more than 10x ... Rox is seeing more than 700% net revenue retention across enterprise customers

key_facts.fact: Rox's AI agents research accounts, prioritize prospects and prepare outreach; customers include Ramp, New Relic, Trafigura, MongoDB and Groq, and it plans to grow its US commercial team fivefold next year.
key_facts.excerpt: Rox's early customers include high-profile firms like Ramp, New Relic, Trafigura, MongoDB, Groq ... Rox plans to expand its U.S. sales, marketing, and commercial team fivefold next year.

key_facts.fact: The rival Rox must beat is Salesforce's Agentforce, which Salesforce puts past $1.5 billion in ARR.
key_facts.excerpt: Rox will grow its US commercial team fivefold next year to take on Agentforce, which Salesforce puts past $1.5 billion in ARR.
